passage: Honestly, the best part was the walk down the corridor. People slowed down to see where I'd sit. I'm Irfan, I was fifteen, and I ran the back table. If a new kid came near, I'd say, "Seat's taken," and watch who noticed. It felt like holding a remote control. But at night I checked my phone for messages, sure that one wrong joke would make them all turn on me. That's what I was really doing, guarding a seat I was scared to lose. One Thursday Pooja came in alone with her lunch box. Everyone looked at me. My throat went dry. I moved my bag and said, "Pooja, here." Nobody said a word. Then Karan asked her about her lunch. Funny thing, the table didn't fall apart. It got bigger.

qa.q: What did Irfan say to a new kid who came near the back table?
qa.a: Irfan said, "Seat's taken," and watched who noticed.

qa.q: What was Irfan really feeling underneath the power?
qa.a: Fear. Irfan checked the phone at night, sure that one wrong joke would make them all turn on Irfan, and was guarding a seat Irfan was scared to lose.

qa.q: How did Irfan use his influence in a better way?
qa.a: Irfan moved the bag and invited Pooja to sit, which made room instead of shutting someone out.

qa.q: How might Pooja have seen Irfan's "Pooja, here"?
qa.a: She probably felt relief and surprise, since she came in alone and everyone looked at Irfan before Irfan spoke. 😊

grounding: Irfan enjoys deciding who is in and out while privately fearing his place, and later uses his influence to include someone.

passage:
Games teacher's observation, Class 9, Monday
Minakshi chose teams again today. She spent a long time choosing, looking around to see who was watching. She picked her friends first and left Zainab to last, saying "Fine, we'll take her," loudly. Several girls laughed. Minakshi smiled at that.
But when Leena, from her own group, started choosing faster and more popular girls on her team, Minakshi went tense and snapped at her twice.
After class I asked Minakshi to walk with me to the equipment room. I told her I'd noticed that people follow her lead. She shrugged, pleased. I asked what she was afraid of losing. She took a long time. "My place," she said. "If I don't choose, someone else will."
I asked her to choose teams on Wednesday so that nobody is last. She agreed, reluctantly. I'll watch how it goes and check in with Zainab too.

qa.q: What did Minakshi say loudly when she picked Zainab?
What was Minakshi afraid of, according to the note?
qa.a: She feared losing her place; she enjoyed people watching her, but felt threatened when Leena started choosing more popular girls.

qa.q: How did the note-writer try to redirect Minakshi's influence?
qa.a: By naming her influence, asking what she feared, and asking her to use it on Wednesday so nobody is picked last.

qa.q: What is it like for Zainab when she is picked last with that comment?
qa.a: Zainab likely feels humiliated and unwanted, especially as others laugh at the comment.

grounding: A teen leader enjoys controlling who is in and out, fears losing her place, and is guided by a teacher to use influence to include.

passage:
Saturday
I'll be honest here because nobody else reads this. I love being the one who decides.
Today at the football ground, the whole group waited for me to say who's on which side. I said Francis sits out. He looked at me like I was the judge. And everyone just went along. That feeling is like standing on a stage.
But here's the thing I don't say. Every time Dev cracks a joke that gets more laughs than mine, I get this cold feeling. What if they start waiting for Dev instead? What if one day I'm the one sitting out?
Francis sat on the wall for the whole match. He left early.
If people listen to me, I could use it differently. Next Saturday I'm going to make the teams fair and put Francis on mine. Lokesh the judge can be Lokesh the captain instead.

qa.q: Who did Lokesh tell to sit out?
What is Lokesh worried about underneath the power?
qa.a: Lokesh feels afraid of losing that place in the group to Dev, and of one day being the one who sits out.

qa.q: What is Lokesh planning to do next Saturday, and why is it a wise use of influence?
qa.a: Lokesh plans to make the teams fair and put Francis on Lokesh's own team, using influence to include rather than to exclude.

qa.q: What was the match like for Francis?
qa.a: Francis probably felt rejected and humiliated, sitting on the wall for the whole match and leaving early.

grounding: A teen who enjoys deciding who is in or out admits a fear of losing that place and decides to use influence to include.
